gen-silkscreen-gf-m-plus-1p: M PLUS 1p reads open at every curve end, tidy and unfussy. Silkscreen is the one for chunky pixel-like outlines drawn in a single width, while M PLUS 1p does best at making text feel easy.
gen-silkscreen-gf-m-plus-2: Retro pixel bluntness up top, friendly roundness below. And Silkscreen with M PLUS 2 gives a lo-fi heading a body whose gaping c shapes stay inviting.
gen-silkscreen-gf-m-plus-code-latin: Silkscreen spaces every letter apart, like spaghetti laid out in rows. It handles bold retro headings best, while M PLUS Code Latin, with sans-serif forms like bent neon tubing, takes over for the running text.
gen-silkscreen-gf-m-plus-rounded-1c: Silkscreen draws straight-edged letters with no pinched joints or flared ends, a lo-fi retro look from top to bottom. M PLUS Rounded 1c is a plain sans that goes down gently.
gen-silkscreen-gf-mandali: Silkscreen draws every stroke at one thickness, with room around each letter you can nearly feel. But Mandali, with its generous entry into the e, makes a longer read go smoothly.
gen-silkscreen-gf-manjari: Retro and lo-fi, Silkscreen leads with spaced-out letters like spaghetti laid in rows. Manjari is a plain sans with wide, unclosed curves, and it holds up better if the heading shrinks and the body grows.
gen-silkscreen-gf-meera-inimai: Meera Inimai reads with open-ended curves and room to breathe, like blueprint lettering. And Silkscreen's lo-fi retro spacing against that line makes the pair feel approachable and distinct.
gen-silkscreen-gf-mina: Silkscreen brings lo-fi, retro spacing, every letter set apart like spaghetti. Mina follows with sans-serif strokes plain as stitched thread outlines, and that contrast is the pair's best quality.
gen-silkscreen-gf-mingzat: Contemporary, with a retro wink. Mingzat's curvy, unclamped letters make a longer passage flow easily under Silkscreen's laser-cut heading look.
gen-silkscreen-gf-moderustic: Moderustic reads modern, its curves traced with a broad nib and left open. Silkscreen's straight-edged, constant strokes would feel cramped if the heading shrank, while a plain sans body like this one can grow.
